clue.text: Presumably wanting pounds set aside for schemes

definitions.meaning: someone who wants the imperial pound abandoned is, presumably, in favour of metric weights
plans or projects to be carried out

explanation.surface: Someone wants money put by for various schemes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pounds' looks like money; here it is the weight, and someone who wants it dropped is presumably pro-grammes. 'for' links the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: plans of action or schedules of planned activities.

clue.text: Foundation's heartless automaton

definitions.note: read as 'foundation is', the definition plus a link

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter is removed

parts.note: a robot is an automaton

explanation.surface: The foundation of the institution is a soulless machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a source or basis from which something grows.

clue.text: Blooming animal out at midday going the wrong way

indicators.note: in a down clue this means reading the letters upwards

parts.note: Noel Coward's song says mad dogs and Englishmen go out in the midday sun

explanation.surface: A flowering creature strays the wrong way in the noon heat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blooming' looks like flowering; it is the mild expletive.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild intensifying curses, as in a blooming nuisance.

clue.text: Object when the French revolutionary leads Parliament

indicators.note: leads puts the reversed article in front
revolutionary means turned round, so these letters are reversed

parts.note: la is the French feminine for the
a thing is an object

explanation.surface: Someone objects when the French radical heads the legislature.
explanation.definitionFit: The Althing is the national parliament of Iceland, one of the oldest in the world.

clue.text: Way in which number is cut by 99% – that's progress

indicators.note: the Roman numeral 500 cut by 99 per cent leaves 5, so that numeral changes to the one for five

parts.note: a mode is the way in which something is done

explanation.surface: A method in which a figure is slashed almost entirely counts as progress.
explanation.walkthrough: The number in MODE is D (500); cut by 99% it becomes 5, V.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to advance or make headway.

clue.text: Unhealthily thin son getting terribly wan in expression of pain

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the cry

parts.note: a cry is an expression of pain

indicators.note: terribly signals the letters of wan are jumbled

explanation.surface: A gaunt son, looking dreadfully pale, cries out in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' turns WAN into AWN, which goes 'in' CRY.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: skinny and bony, lean to an unhealthy degree.

clue.text: Observed heading north on cruise maybe and celebrating in song

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above the next part
in a down clue heading north means reading upwards

parts.note: saw means observed
a cruise is one kind of sailing

explanation.surface: Seen sailing north on a cruise, singing merrily.
explanation.definitionFit: Wassailing is going from house to house singing carols and drinking healths.

clue.text: Those interpreting second book of scripture — Bible-bashers, say?

parts.note: Ex is the abbreviation for Exodus, the second book of the Bible
those who bash, thump or hammer things are pounders

explanation.surface: Evangelical preachers explain the second book of the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' and the question mark flag that bashers are pounders only by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who explain or set out the meaning of something in detail.

clue.text: Socialist hit back wanting favourable sign at the polls

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for hit from right to left

parts.note: to ram is to hit hard
a voter marks a cross beside the candidate they support

explanation.surface: A left-winger strikes back after failing to win votes.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: Karl Marx, the founder of modern communism, was a socialist thinker.

clue.text: Rule books of old one doctor rejected when hugged by sweetheart

indicators.note: being hugged by something means being held inside it

parts.note: a lover is a sweetheart

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so this string is read backwards

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, the old books of the Bible
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A doctor turns down old books while a sweetheart embraces him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rule' looks like a noun; it is the verb. 'rejected' reverses the inner string to RDITO before 'when hugged by' wraps the sweetheart round it.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: to domineer or behave in a lordly, overbearing way over someone.

clue.text: Noble philosopher surprisingly let off

indicators.note: off says these letters are taken away from the philosopher's name

parts.note: Aristotle, the Greek philosopher
the letters of let in a surprising order, as they end the philosopher's name

explanation.surface: A noble thinker has unexpectedly been released.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' rearranges LET to TLE, the last three letters of ARISTOTLE, and 'off' removes them.
explanation.definitionFit: A clipped informal form of aristocrat, a member of the nobility.

clue.text: Maiden taking chaps into bed brings criticism

indicators.note: taking chaps into bed places them inside the word for bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
M is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for a maiden over
chaps are men

explanation.surface: A young woman's habit of taking men to bed draws disapproval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' takes both the maiden and the chaps inside the bed; a maiden is a cricket over with no runs scored.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a remark, especially a critical or evaluative one.

clue.text: A bit icy, pal — awkward for a gardener to show skill

indicators.note: awkward suggests the letters sit clumsily and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener finds frosty weather awkward when showing off expertise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a gardener to show' points to Capability Brown, the 18th-century English landscape gardener.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: ability or competence to do something.

clue.text: This person's suffering penning diary, one scientist beset by mouldy items?

parts.note: the setter refers to himself; his is my

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the suffering word wraps the diary and one

parts.note: cost means loss or suffering, as in to one's cost
a log is a diary or record
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: The setter suffers while keeping a journal, a scientist surrounded by mould.
explanation.definitionFit: A mycologist studies fungi, including moulds.

clue.text: Figure of speech used by reporter in write-up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means reading the letters upwards
used by points to letters found within the word

explanation.surface: A journalist uses a figure of speech in an article.
explanation.definitionFit: A trope is a figurative use of a word, such as a metaphor.

clue.text: Social event — female exuded oiliness

indicators.note: exuded means oozed out, so the letter for female leaves the word

parts.note: a function is a formal social gathering

explanation.surface: At a party, a woman gave off an air of smarm.
explanation.definitionFit: Unction means unctuousness: an oily, ingratiating manner, or literally an ointment.

clue.text: Some of Iris's superior meat

definitions.note: relating to a part of the eye that includes the iris

parts.note: U means upper class or superior
veal is calf meat

explanation.surface: A woman called Iris has some top-quality meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iris' looks like a woman's name; it is part of the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The uvea is the eye's pigmented layer including the iris, so uveal means belonging to it.

clue.text: Something saucy — it is lacking in seriousness

indicators.note: lacking in means without, so the word it is removed

parts.note: gravity is seriousness or solemnity

explanation.surface: Something cheeky lacks any solemnity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saucy' suggests cheekiness; it means literally sauce-like.
explanation.definitionFit: Gravy is a sauce made from meat juices, so literally something saucy.

clue.text: Put in suitcase four suits

definitions.meaning: to put clothes into luggage for a trip
a deck of cards contains four suits

explanation.surface: Stowing four suits in a suitcase for a trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb for loading luggage and a noun for a deck of playing cards.

clue.text: Weapon giving power to US President once

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for power in physics
Ike was the nickname of Dwight Eisenhower, US President in the 1950s

explanation.surface: A weapon gives power to a former American president.
explanation.definitionFit: A pike is a long infantry spear, an example of a weapon.

clue.text: Row across river — you'll see fish

indicators.note: the row is placed across the river letter, so it surrounds it

parts.note: a spat is a quarrel or row

explanation.surface: Rowing over a river, you will spot fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like using oars; it is a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprat is a small sea fish of the herring family.

clue.text: Tricky situation — I caught a beastly disease

indicators.note: the tricky situation has caught the letter, so holds it inside

parts.note: a scrape is an awkward predicament

explanation.surface: In an awkward spot, someone catches a nasty illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrapie is a fatal brain disease of sheep and goats, so an animal disease.

clue.text: Restrict diet now if it's bad

indicators.note: bad suggests the letters are in poor order and need rearranging

explanation.surface: Restrict your eating now if things are bad.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb: to tie down is to confine or limit someone.

clue.text: Pope's pronouncement gets a church bearing fruit

parts.note: a papal bull is a formal decree from the Pope
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A papal edict yields a church bearing fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The bullace is a wild plum, a small dark fruit.

clue.text: Westward journey beset by trees in French city

indicators.note: being beset by something means being surrounded by it

parts.note: limes are trees, also called lindens

indicators.note: in an across clue westward means reading right to left

parts.note: a go can be a turn or trip

explanation.surface: A westbound trip among trees in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Westward' reverses the journey to OG, and 'beset by' puts it among the trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Limoges is a city in central France famous for porcelain.

clue.text: Eight special days bringing a victory at end of month

indicators.note: at end of puts the a and the victory after the month

parts.note: Oct is the abbreviation for October
VE stands for Victory in Europe, as in VE Day

explanation.surface: A victory at month's end is celebrated for eight special days.
explanation.definitionFit: In the church calendar an octave is the eight-day period following a major feast.

clue.text: Insensitive person, soldier at front of a covered arcade

indicators.note: at front of places the soldier ahead of the letter a

parts.note: someone as unfeeling as a log of wood
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: An unfeeling man and a soldier stand at the front of an arcade.
explanation.definitionFit: A loggia is a gallery or arcade open on one side, an architectural term.

clue.text: River in painting on wall but not ceiling

indicators.note: in a down clue the ceiling is the top letter, which is dropped

parts.note: a mural is a painting on a wall

explanation.surface: A river appears in a wall painting but not on the ceiling.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ural is a river flowing from the Ural Mountains to the Caspian Sea.

clue.text: Rowdy person born in the late Forties? Not Giovanni

indicators.note: not tells us the setter is excluded from the word

parts.note: a baby boomer was born in the postwar birth surge
Giovanni is the setter, who refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: A rowdy postwar baby, but not the setter himself.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a rude, ill-mannered, uncouth person.

clue.text: A fine speaker? One may be boring

parts.note: per means a, as in 'a pound per kilo'
F is the abbreviation for fine, on pencil leads
an orator is a public speaker

explanation.surface: Is a fine orator someone who might send people to sleep?
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' suggests tedium; it means drilling holes.
explanation.definitionFit: A perforator is a tool or machine that bores or punches holes.

clue.text: Second drunkard to fall back and roll around

indicators.note: falling back means the letters run in reverse

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunk

explanation.surface: A second drunk topples over and rolls about.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to toss is to roll about restlessly, as in tossing and turning.

clue.text: Actress, see, keeping time of holy observance before sin

indicators.note: keeping means holding within, so the see word surrounds the rest

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city and bishop's see in Cambridgeshire

indicators.note: before puts the holy season ahead of the sin

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting
to err is to sin

explanation.surface: An actress, watch, observes Lent before sinning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' looks like a verb; in crosswords it is often a bishop's diocese. 'keeping' holds the season and the sin within it.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: Ellen Terry was a celebrated Victorian Shakespearean actress.
